sn40.4:0.3: A Question About the Fourth Absorption
sn40.4:1.1: “They speak of this thing called the ‘fourth stage of meditation’.
sn40.4:1.2: What is the fourth stage of meditation?
sn40.4:1.4: ‘It’s when, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a bhikkhu enters and dwells in the fourth stage of meditation, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and awareness.
sn40.4:1.5: This is called the fourth stage of meditation.’
sn40.4:1.6: And so … I was entering and remaining in the fourth stage of meditation.
sn40.4:1.7: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by pleasure beset me.
sn40.4:2.1: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,
sn40.4:2.3: Don’t neglect the fourth stage of meditation, brahmin! Settle your mind in the fourth stage of meditation; unify your mind and concentrate it in the fourth stage of meditation.’
sn40.4:2.4: And so, after some time … I entered and dwelled in the fourth stage of meditation.
sn40.4:2.5: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”
